programs.title: Treehouse Masters
programs.desc: Pete Nelson uproots an existing treehouse from the family-owned bed & breakfast Treehouse Point to build a custom-made treehouse as a housewarming gift for his daughter, Emily.

programs.title: Treehouse Masters
programs.desc: Pete pushes his design skills to create an owl-inspired tree house library in Charlotte, N.C.; evoking the face of the bird and using all sorts of curves, including rounded walls and semi-circle bookcases, the crew builds a one-of-a-kind masterpiece.

programs.title: Treehouse Masters
programs.desc: Pete and his team undertake a sticky challenge and reinvent the classic single-tree treehouse; constructing a magnificent and whimsical beehive-like structure soaring 30-feet high in a majestic Douglas fir.

programs.title: Barnwood Builders
programs.desc: Mark brings one of his biggest ideas to life -- a foldable steel cabin; the crew takes the cabin on its maiden voyage and unfolds it for the first time in the bone-yard, then they add a timber frame facade and a barn-wood interior.

programs.title: Barnwood Builders
programs.sub_title: Fancy Cabin Takedown in Minor Hill
programs.desc: Mark Bowe and his crew work through layers of architectural history to uncover an original pioneer home in Minor Hill, Tenn., while hearing stories from family members who lived in the cabin; Mark visits a beautifully restored log home.

programs.title: Second Chance Stage
programs.desc: On the eve of finale, the judges choose between six performances, including a jump rope team, dancers, stand-ups and a jazz crooner.
